barriers.reason: A 5:30 AM in-center start likely precedes fixed-route bus/rail service, and the patient is already weak/tired and has missed four sessions this month; ADA paratransit cannot cover trips earlier than fixed-route hours and requires certification first.

alternatives.text: Ask the dialysis unit for a later chair time or a different day that matches an available ride, framing it as a request given limited chair times.

Assess eligibility and apply for ADA Paratransit certification (Northern Illinois Transit Authority, 312-663-HELP); note it is not immediate and cannot serve a 5:30 AM trip if no fixed route runs then.
Have the unit social worker (already asked to check in) help arrange transport and benefits for in-center dialysis.

barriers.reason: The diet handout is in English while the patient needs Polish; the daughter in Arizona reads it by phone but works, so translated support is unreliable.

alternatives.text: Use the hospital interpreter service and provide plain-language, translated (Polish) renal diet instructions.
Ask the dialysis unit dietitian to rebuild the low-potassium diet around foods the patient can actually obtain and provide Polish-language materials.
